jobs.occupation: Senior Engineer
jobs.description:
About the position
A permanent position as Senior engineer (position code 1181) is available at The Department of Physics, University of Oslo.

Starting date as soon as possible. 

Place of work is Department of Physics at Blindern, Oslo.
Job description and work tasks
The Electronics section has seven academic positions (two full-time and five part-time) and two technical positions. The research activity is currently largely related to projects in medical technology, particularly those using methods based on impedance spectroscopy. The successful candidate may also provide technical support for new research activities in electronic components and neuromorphic electronics, especially related to electrical characterization, measurement setups, and laboratory infrastructure. 

Together with the Department of Informatics, the section is responsible for a study program in electronics, informatics, and technology. The academic staff are therefore responsible for several courses in electronics and sensor technology and also contribute to teaching basic physics courses. The section’s staff are also involved in the supervision of students at both master’s and doctoral level. 

The engineering position is intended to support both the research and teaching activities in which the section is involved. 

The tasks connected to teaching will primarily involve training and assisting master’s and PhD students in the use of specialized measuring instruments and software. 

Part of the position also involves organizing the section’s student laboratories. This includes testing of hardware and software, as well as other typical engineering tasks related to the day to-day operation of the laboratories.
What skills are important in this role?
Qualification requirements:

The minimum educational requirement is a master’s degree (or equivalent) in electronics/electrical engineering. In addition, the candidate must have experience with: 

• Instrumentation, measurement systems, and laboratory work 
• Impedance spectroscopy and interpretation of bioimpedance data 
• Programming in Python and MATLAB, or equivalent 
• Finite element modelling, e.g. COMSOL Multiphysics 
• Good oral and written English skills
The following qualifications are strongly desirable and will be emphasized in the evaluation process: 

• Research experience, preferably demonstrated through a PhD degree 
• Use of various sensors for monitoring food quality, such as colorimetry, pH measurements, and NIR spectrometry 
• Electrical characterization of semiconductor devices or other electronic components, preferably including low-current and/or pulsed measurements 
• Automation and integration of laboratory instruments and measurement systems 
• Technical supervision of studentsWhat are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• A service minded attitude 
• Ability to work independently 
• Ability to work precisely in a structured and solution-oriented manner and swiftly adapts to new tasks 
• Good communication and collaboration skills 
• Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods 
• Have a safety-oriented attitude
Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal skills.
We can offer you
• A pleasant and stimulating work environment
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
• Salary in position as Senior Engineer, position code 1181 in salary range NOK 700 000 – 775 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2% is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension FundWe need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We especially encourage women to apply.We hope you will apply for the position with us.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Cover letter with a statement of motivation
• CV (complete overview of education and work experience)
• Copies of educational certificates and transcript of records
• Names and contact details of 2-3 references (names, relation to candidate and telephone number)
Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
Formal regulations
The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Integrative Global Change Biology
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you a motivated researcher who wants to take a step towards a doctorate degree? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will join a vibrant evolutionary ecology group, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research.

Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department.
About the project
We are looking for a PhD candidate to be part of an interdisciplinary team investigating geographic variation in how European insects cope with the combined stress of higher temperatures and drier conditions. There is growing evidence that insect populations are declining around the world, making the proposed research timely and important.

This project builds on research comparing the physiological responses of insect species from contrasting climates to better understand future responses to changes in temperature and precipitation. The PhD position will be focused primarily on understanding the plastic and evolved responses of insects to temperature and hydric stress. The expected research will include a combination of field and lab work, including insect husbandry, and physiological experiments characterizing thermal and desiccation tolerance. The position will require statistical analyses and potentially the development of eco-evolutionary biophysical models. The results of this work are expected to be disseminated in the scientific literature as well as to the public and relevant stakeholders. The primary supervisor for this position will be Professor Cameron Ghalambor. 
Duties of the position
• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the Biodiversity, Ecology, and Evolution research group as part of the Ghalambor lab 
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions
• Teaching experience in courses related to Ecology and Evolution
Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD programme in Biology, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in biology or equivalent with relevant background in evolutionary biology, ecology, entomology, physiology, or similar. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis
• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than December 2026.
• You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
• You have excellent written and oral English language skills 
• You have some experience conducting statistical analyses using R or other statistical languages.
The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• You have experience conducting field and lab research with insects, or a willingness to learn 
• You have the ability to collect data in rigorous, repeatable, and transparent way
• You have good data management skills
• You have demonstrated strong quantitative & analytical skills
• You can code in R, Python, and or other statistical languages
• You can demonstrate strong scientific writing skills
• You can demonstrate the ability to complete tasks in a timely manner
• You work well in a collaborative environmentPersonal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

• Be passionate about pursuing knowledge and scholarship in your field
• Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them
• Present and discuss your research with other professionals
• Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback
• Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity 
• Have a strong motivation to read and be familiar with the primary literature
• Be able to interpret results and draw well-founded conclusions 
• Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed
• Communicate effectively in writing, speaking, and public presentations 
• Work well as part of a team with diverse research interests
• Be self-motivated and enthusiastic about your research topic and for dissemination of scientific research, both through journal articles and public engagement
Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.
We offer
Evaluate and remove/add what is relevant for the position.

• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work with the possibility of up to 1 year of career promoting work. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Biology  within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.

 
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English or with a certified English translation. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

• A one-page cover letter stating specifically why you believe you meet the selection criteria
• A 1-2 page summary of your motivation for pursuing a PhD, research interests, past experience, future research goals, and why you think you are a good fit for this position.
• CV, certificates and diplomas

• A copy of the master's thesis. If you recently have submitted your master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed master's degree must be presented before taking up the position. 
• Name and address of three referees 
• If you have publications, other relevant research work that demonstrate your writing skills
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. 

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

 

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

 
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Cameron Ghalambor cameron.ghalambor@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Maja Haaker maja.haaker@ntnu.no.

 

Application deadline: 03.01.2027

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral positions in Labour Economics
jobs.description:
About the positions
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applications for two postdoctoral positions in applied microeconomics at the Department of Economics. The duration of each position is three years.The postdoctoral positions offer a unique opportunity to join an ambitious research environment in applied microeconomics and to become an integral part of the FAIR- Centre for Experimental Research on Fairness, Inequality and Rationality and the Department Economics (FAIR) at the Department of Economics. The successful candidates will work closely with researchers at FAIR on one of two research projects:Postdoctoral Position 1: FOUNDATIONS: The Foundations of Labor ProductivityThe FOUNDATIONS project is funded by the European Research Council (Project 101302557). The successful candidate will work closely with Alexander Willén and other researchers on projects examining how labor-market structures shape worker sorting and learning, firm strategy, workplace organisation, and productivity. The research combines large-scale surveys and experiments with population-wide administrative data and detailed firm-level information, with a particular focus on questions related to market power, human capital, and productivity.

Postdoctoral Position 2: Labor-Market Structures, Working Conditions, and Worker Well-BeingThis project is funded by NFR Fripro grant 360300. The successful candidate will work closely with Katrine Løken and Alexander Willén, and other researchers at FAIR on projects examining how labor-market structures and institutions shape working conditions and workers’ broader life outcomes. The research will combine rich administrative data, linked survey data, and empirical methods to study questions related to employer power, worker voice and unions, workplace environment, and worker well-being.

Both positions provide substantial scope for intellectual contribution and for developing independent research within the respective research agendas.We are looking for highly ambitious and collaborative researchers with a strong background in applied microeconomics, particularly labor, public, personnel, or organisational economics. The ideal candidates will have excellent empirical, analytical, and technical skills and combine methodological rigor with creativity and a strong motivation to produce research aimed at publication in leading international journals.The department seeks ambitious candidates early in their careers. Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD degree in a business-oriented field such as economics or a closely related field from a recognised business school or university.
NHH offers
• Competitive terms depending on the level of competence/length of service.
• An academically stimulating working environment.
• A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
• Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild, coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities - as well as a family-friendly environment (explore visitnorway.com).

The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers, a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right side. 
 
Two or three reference letters (in PDF) must be submitted by the referees directly to NHH at hr-references@nhh.no, by latest 22 December 2026. As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent. In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted. 

Enquiries about the positions may be directed to:

• Professor Alexander Willén, by email: alexander.willen@nhh.no
• Professor Katrine Løken, by email: katrine.loken@nhh.no
• Administrative coordinator Mette Soltvedt, by email mette.soltvedt@nhh.no

jobs.occupation: Researcher in host–microbiome interactions in human liver diseases
jobs.description:
About the position
Do you want to work as a researcher in the field of host-microbiome interactions in human liver disease funded by the ERC?

One position is available as Researcher (SKO1109) - a temporary 3-year position - at Research Institute of Internal Medicine at Institute of Clinical Medicine, funded by an ERC/ European Research Council Consolidator grant.

Research Institute of Internal Medicine at the Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo, is physically located at Rikshospitalet, Oslo University Hospital, and consists of 6 research groups, and a total of about 60 employees. The research profile of the Institute is to combine clinical medicine and molecular biology to establish a bridge between bench and bedside. This is of utmost importance to exploit in clinical medicine the recent development in immunology, biochemistry and molecular biology with the ambitious aim of developing novel treatment modalities and new diagnostic tools.

Integrated in the institute is the Norwegian PSC Research Center (NoPSC), which is a world-leading center dedicated to research on the chronic liver disease primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). About the position
We invite applications for a three-year PhD Research Fellow position in experimental proton therapy, available at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo (UiO).

The preferred starting date is March 1, 2027, and no later than April 1, 2027.The fellowship period is 36 months.

The position is part of InnovaRTBRAIN – Innovative Radiation Therapy for Brain Tumors, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) funded by the European Union. The network brings together leading European research institutions, hospitals, and industrial partners to develop innovative radiation therapy approaches for brain tumors, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma.The successful candidate will be recruited as Doctoral Candidate 13 (DC13) and will join the proton therapy research group at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo and the Department of Radiation Biology, Oslo University Hospital (OUS).

Most of the experimental research will be carried out at the proton therapy facility at Oslo University Hospital, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for preclinical proton irradiation, including a dedicated research beamline and gantry, a 3T small-animal MRI scanner, and facilities for experimental radiobiology.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo. 
Background of the project
Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive forms of brain cancer, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Radiation therapy plays a central role in its treatment, but its effectiveness is restricted by tumor radioresistance and the sensitivity of surrounding healthy brain tissue.

Proton minibeam radiation therapy (pMBRT) is an emerging approach in which radiation is delivered in narrow, spatially separated beams, producing a highly heterogeneous dose distribution. This technique has the potential to reduce radiation-induced damage to healthy tissues while maintaining effective tumor irradiation. However, its biological effects, particularly the evolution of tumor and normal tissue responses over time, remain incompletely understood. 
 
The PhD project will investigate the biological response to proton minibeam irradiation in preclinical models of brain cancer, using longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and quantitative image analysis. The project will also explore the potential of MRI-derived biomarkers for assessing treatment response and normal tissue effects. An important part of the research will be conducted in close collaboration with another doctoral candidate in InnovaRTBRAIN (DC6), based at Oslo University Hospital, who will investigate combinations of radiation therapy and immunotherapy, including CAR-T cell treatment.
Job description 
The doctoral candidate will conduct experimental studies in mouse models to investigate tumor and normal tissue responses to proton minibeam radiation therapy, using magnetic resonance imaging and other methods to characterize radiation-induced biological effects.The main responsibilities will be:

• Plan and conduct preclinical proton minibeam irradiation experiments in mouse models
• Acquire and analyze MRI data, including diffusion-weighted imaging, to quantify treatment response and potential normal tissue toxicity
• Relate MR-derived image parameters to radiation dose distributions, linear energy transfer (LET), and biological endpoints
• Develop and apply quantitative image analysis and radiomics methods to identify imaging features associated with tumor response and radiation injury
• Investigate MRI-based biomarkers in combination with NMR-derived metabolic and relaxation-time markers, in collaboration with international project partners
• Collaborate with DC6 on preclinical studies combining proton minibeam radiation therapy and immunotherapy
• Participate in joint research, training activities, and research visits within the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network Research environment
The candidate will join an interdisciplinary research environment combining radiobiology, medical physics, experimental proton therapy, and medical imaging. The research will be conducted in close collaboration between the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital, primarily at the proton therapy research facility at the Norwegian Radium Hospital. The facility provides access to experimental proton irradiation, a dedicated small-animal MRI scanner, treatment planning software, and infrastructure for preclinical cancer research.
Supervisors and international collaboration
The doctoral candidate will be supervised by Professor Eirik Malinen (UiO/OUS), with co-supervision from Professor Nina Edin (UiO), Professor Paul Vasos (University of Bucharest), and Else Marit Inderberg (OUS). The InnovaRTBRAIN network will provide an international and interdisciplinary training environment, combining expertise in medical physics, radiobiology, imaging, cancer biology, and immunotherapy.
Planned secondments
As part of the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network, the candidate will undertake research visits to international academic and industrial partners:

• University of Bucharest, Romania (3 months): Integration of NMR-based biomarkers with MRI-derived radiomics to characterize tumor responses.
• Xstrahl, UK (2 weeks): Training in small-animal irradiation technologies and their applications in preclinical radiation therapy research.
• COSYLAB, Slovenia (2 weeks): Exposure to industrial developments in radiation therapy technology and control systems.
These secondments will provide complementary scientific and technical training and strengthen collaboration within the InnovaRTBRAIN network.

Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network GLASS-CARE, collaborate with academic, museums, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on cultural heritage science.

As part of the GLASS-CARE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. About the project
About the GLASS-CARE project GLASS-CARE (Green Light for Advanced Solutions in Stained-glass Conservation and Application of Research and Education) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, GLASS-CARE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation. For more details, visit http://www.glasscare.eu/

About the DC projectWithin the GLASS-CARE project, the individual research project associated with this position (DC13) is entitled Multi-sensor data fusion for digital representation.

The PhD project will investigate computational approaches for integrating data acquired through hyperspectral imaging (HSI), multispectral imaging (MSI), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), and photoacoustic techniques.

The resulting computational framework will contribute to improved material characterization, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making for historical stained glass.The PhD candidate will address the following objectives (1) Multimodal data integration (2) Multimodal registration, alignment and data fusion (3) Feature extraction and dimensionality reduction (4) Unified digital representations (6) Validation through case studies.

Expected results: (1)  A computational framework for integrating heterogeneous imaging and analytical data into unified digital representations of stained glass. (2) Advanced data fusion methods to minimize redundancy, preserve complementary information, and reveal hidden patterns across different imaging modalities. (3) Deliver validated computational models and tools for improved material characterization, visualisation, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making.

jobs.employer_name: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
jobs.description:
The position
The Faculty of Law has a position vacant for applicants who wish to obtain the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD). The position is affiliated with the Norwegian Centre for the Law of the Sea (NCLOS).

The position is for a period of four years. The nominal length of the PhD programme is three years. The fourth year is distributed as 25 % each year and will consist of teaching and other duties. The objective of the position is to complete research training to the level of a doctoral degree. Admission to the PhD programme is a prerequisite for employment, and the programme period starts on commencement of the position.The PhD fellow shall participate in the faculty’s organized research training, and the PhD project shall be completed during the period of employment.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.
The Faculty of Law and NCLOS
The Faculty of Law has about 1000 law students, 25 PhD students, 40 members of the academic staff, and 18 members of the administrative staff. The Faculty may award the degrees of Master and PhD in Law as well as the degrees of Master of Laws (LL.M.) in the Law of the Sea and Joint Nordic Master`s Programme in Environmental Law. For more information about the faculty, see our website The Faculty of Law.

NCLOS has a staff of 20 - 25 employees; academic staff and PhD fellows. The Centre is located at the Faculty of Law, providing for close contact and collaboration between the staff. The Centre also has an extensive national and international academic network. NCLOS has been awarded status as UiT Aurora Centre 2021 - 25. More information on NCLOS and the UiT Aurora Centre, see our website: www.uit.no/lawofthesea
The position’s field of research
The position is affiliated with the national research program Arctic Ocean 2050. The program brings together 18 Norwegian research institutions in a major interdisciplinary collaboration aimed at strengthening Norway’s knowledge base and strategic capacity in a rapidly changing Arctic Ocean. Its goals are to improve our understanding of the present-day Arctic Ocean and how it may change towards 2050, and develop the knowledge needed for future management, sustainable use, and a safe and secure region. The ten-year program (2026–2035) combines basic research, applied science, and innovation – offering unique opportunities for professional development and cross-disciplinary collaboration.Arctic Ocean 2050 focuses on processes within the central Arctic Ocean, its interactions with the surrounding seas, and how these dynamics connect to broader climatic and political systems. Field activities will primarily take place in the Eurasian Basin, between Fram Strait and the North Pole, as well as including the adjacent continental slopes. Pan-Arctic perspectives will be ensured through remote sensing, research on broader sociopolitical drivers, and modelling tools that cover the entire Arctic Ocean, and extensive international research collaboration.As part of Arctic Ocean 2050, you will join an ambitious research environment with high societal relevance and the opportunity to contribute to new knowledge on some of the world’s most remote and important ocean regions.In this context, NCLOS seeks to fill one PhD position to contribute to the NCLOS research at the intersection of global and regional regimes, with particular focus on the Arctic.Projects addressing one or more of the following themes will be preferred:

• The Arctic law and governance regime complex, and the interactions among existing legal instruments frameworks and bodies in times of geopolitical shifts
• Sustainable conservation of Arctic resources, living or non-living, in the context of climatic changes
• Critical Arctic infrastructures and Law of the Sea
• Arctic Geopolitics and its impact on the legal order of the sea
• Regulating a “blue” Arctic Ocean across sectors through ecosystem-based conservation
• Regulating future Arctic shipping
• The role of the BBNJ agreement in the Arctic 
Projects taking a doctrinal, contextual or critical theoretical and methodological approaches are equally welcome.The candidate selected for employment must be willing to adjust her/his project proposals to the plans of the Centre.
Qualifications 
The successful applicants must fulfil the requirements for admission to the Faculty's PhD programme. Information about requirements is available here.

The applicants must have a five years Master’s degree in Law or Cand. jur. with good grades. The Faculty may accept equivalent education in law from foreign universities.

The applicants must present a description outlining the academic basis of the PhD project. The project description shall be 5-8 pages, and must include an overview of the topic, main and sub-research questions for the project, a justification of these choices, and literature references. It shall also indicate the methodologies to be used. No coverage of expenses related to fieldwork, beyond the allotted annuum, can be expected. The description should also include considerations regarding affiliation with the faculty's research groups/NCLOS. The applicant may be asked to supplement the description.
 
Applicants must document fluency in English language. If the applicant does not have proficiency in Norwegian or a Scandinavian language (level A2), the applicant must commit him-/herself to participate in the Norwegian Language Courses held by the UiT at the outset of the employment

In the assessment, the emphasis is on the applicant's potential to complete a research education based on the master's thesis or equivalent, and any other scientific work. The project description will also be considered. In addition, other experience of significance for the completion of the doctoral programme may be given consideration.

Emphasis will be put on the candidate's potential for research, motivation and personal suitability for the position.

As many as possible should have the opportunity to undertake organized research training. If you already hold a PhD or have equivalent competence, we will not appoint you to this position.
Inclusion and diversity
UiT The Arctic University of Norway is working actively to promote equality, gender balance and diversity among employees and students, and to create an inclusive and safe working environment. We believe that inclusion and diversity are a strength, and we want employees with different competencies, professional experience, life experience and perspectives.

If you have a disability, a gap in your CV or immigrant background, we encourage you to tick the box for this in your application. If there are qualified applicants, we invite at least one in each group for an interview. If you get the job, we will adapt the working conditions if you need it. Apart from selecting the right candidates, we will only use the information for anonymous statistics.
We offer 
• Involvement in an interesting research project
• Good career opportunities, and high employability after successful graduation
• A stunning Arctic landscape and diversity of outdoor activities
• Flexible working hours and a state collective pay agreement 
• Pension scheme through the state pension fund
Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.

More practical information about working and living in Norway can be found here: https://uit.no/staffmobility
Application  
Please note that the application will only be assessed based on the information submitted by the application deadline via Jobbnorge. It is therefore important that you include all necessary documents demonstrating your qualifications for the position.

Your application must include:

• Cover letter explaining your motivation and research interests 
• CV
• Official diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language 
• Official transcripts of grades/academic record for Bachelor's and Master's degree in the original language
• Official translation of diplomas and transcripts of records (ToR) to English or a Scandinavian language, if applicable
• Explanation of the grading system for foreign education (Diploma Supplement if available)
• Documentation of English proficiency
• Documentation of proficiency in Norwegian or a Scandinavian language (level A2) or commit him-/herself to participate in the Norwegian Language Courses held by the UiT at the outset of the employment
• 2-3 references with contact information
• Master’s thesis, and any other academic works 
• Project description (5-8 pages)
• Application for admission
All documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English. If English proficiency is not documented in the application, it must be documented before starting in the position. 

If you have larger academic works that are submitted via link and should be assessed by the evaluation committee, we request that this is explicitly mentioned in the application.
Assessment
The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications based on the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description drawn up for the position. A copy of the assessment report will be sent to all applicants. 

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be invited to an interview. The interview should, among other things, aim to clarify the applicant’s motivation and personal suitability for the position. 
General information
The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants.

A shorter period of appointment may be decided when the PhD Fellow has already completed parts of their research training programme or when the appointment is based on a previous qualifying position PhD Fellow, research assistant, or the like in such a way that the total time used for research training amounts to three years.
 
Remuneration for the position of PhD Fellow is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1017.  A compulsory contribution of 2 % to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted. You will become a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund, which gives you many benefits in addition to a lifelong pension: You may be entitled to financial support if you become ill or disabled, you become insured against occupational injury or occupational disease, and you can get good terms on a mortgage. Read more about your employee benefits at: spk.no. 

We process personal data given in an application or CV in accordance with the Personal Data Act (Offentleglova). According to the Personal Data Act information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure. You will receive advance notification in the event of such publication, if you have requested non-disclosure.

The position
The Norwegian Centre for the Law of the Sea (NCLOS) has an open Postdoctoral Fellow position. 

The position is a fixed term position for a duration of three years. Appointment to the position of Postdoctoral Research Fellow is mainly intended to provide qualification for work in top academic positions. The applicant must be able to carry out the project over the full course ofthe employment period. No person may hold more than one fixed term position as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the same institution.

The position will additionally be assigned to teaching and related work for UiT equivalent to a maximum 20 % of a full-time employment.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.

jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i menneskesentrert evaluering av agentbasert KI
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i menneskesentrert evaluering av agentbasert KI ved Det teknisk- naturvitenskapelige fakultet, Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi. Stillingen er ledig fra våren 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.
 
Den som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i teknologi og naturvitenskap. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.

Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.
Forskningstema
Den som ansettes vil være tilknyttet forskningsprosjektet Menneskesentrert evaluering av agentbasert KI.

KI-agenter har gått raskt fra kun å svare på spørsmål til nå å kunne utføre arbeid i flere trinn på vegne av folk, og referansetestene som er laget for å følge denne utviklingen blir utdaterte nesten like raskt som de publiseres. Evaluering har blitt en flaskehals. Statiske referansetester er verdifulle for å måle en modells evne til å løse en veldefinert oppgave på egen hånd, men de lar en komplementær dimensjon stå stort sett umålt: agentens nytte for personen den skal tjene.

Kunnskapsarbeid i praksis, som informasjonssøk og dataanalyse, starter sjelden med en klar oppgavebeskrivelse. Brukerne finner ut hva de trenger underveis, endrer retning i lys av delresultater, og må hele tiden vurdere hvor mye de kan stole på det agenten forteller dem. Dette prosjektet ser på agenten som en assistent i denne prosessen: en som hjelper brukerne med å formulere problemet, tilpasser seg når målene deres endrer seg, og er åpen nok om egen resonnering, usikkerhet og begrensninger til at brukerne kan avgjøre hvor mye de skal støtte seg til den.

Det overordnede målet er å utvikle evalueringsinstrumenter som fanger opp agentens nytte for menneskelige brukere, og spesielt å muliggjøre forskning på agenters åpenhet som fører til bedre informerte beslutninger. Brukersimulering spiller en sentral rolle. Brukerstudier med mennesker vil kartlegge hva brukerne faktisk trenger og hvordan de oppfører seg. Dette grunnlaget skal brukes til å bygge simulatorer for skiftende mål, ulik ekspertise og atferd knyttet til hvor mye brukerne stoler på agenten, kalibrert og validert mot virkelige brukere. De resulterende referansetestene leveres sammen med disse validerte simulatorene, slik at menneskesentrert evaluering blir skalerbar og reproduserbar.

Forventede bidrag omfatter:

• empiriske innsikter i brukernes behov og i hvor mye de stoler på agenter
• validerte brukersimulatorer og en metodikk for å validere dem mot data fra mennesker
• mål for kvaliteten på samarbeidet og for om agentens åpenhet er tilstrekkelig 
• ressurser for referansetesting og datasett fra brukerstudierKvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor informatikk, datavitenskap, kunstig intelligens, eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato.

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.

Dersom du fullfører mastergraden våren 2027, er du også velkommen til å søke.

Søkere med erfaring innen NLP, informasjonsgjenfinning, maskinlæring, HCI og menneskesentrert databehandling, kognitiv vitenskap eller informasjonsvitenskap foretrekkes.
 
Vi legger også vekt på at du:

• har høy faglig integritet og fokus på kvalitet i arbeidet
• er nysgjerrig og motivert for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og samarbeid på tvers av fagområder
• har potensial for forskning innenfor fagfeltet og personlige forutsetninger for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• kan arbeide godt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• har evne til kritisk refleksjon, nytenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, og arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø.
• har gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig.Krav til engelskkunnskaper

Mangfold og inkludering
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.

Ansettelsesvilkår og videre prosess
UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. På bakgrunn av komiteens vurdering vil aktuelle søkere bli invitert til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater. Les mer om ansettelsesprosessen på våre nettsider.
 
Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den engelske teksten som legges til grunn.

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 2.200 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for grønn og bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjente.

Det teknisk-naturvitenskapelige fakultet tilbyr utdanninger på bachelor-, master- og doktorgradsnivå. Fakultetet har sterke bånd til både forskningsinstitusjoner og industri. Nesten 40 % av budsjettet er eksternt finansiert. Studentene våre har tett kontakt med næringslivet, og mange master- og doktorgradsoppgaver blir skrevet i samarbeid med industrien. Fakultetet har etablert forskningssamarbeid med universiteter over hele verden, og har flere fagmiljø som er internasjonalt ledende. Fakultetet har om lag 3000 studenter og rundt 500 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen og seks institutt: institutt for data- og elektroteknikk, institutt for maskin, bygg og materialteknologi, institutt for matematikk og fysikk, institutt for kjemi, biovitenskap og miljøteknologi, institutt for energi- og petroleumsteknologi og institutt for sikkerhet, økonomi og planlegging. Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi driver forskning innen datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, elkraft, signalbehandling og medisinsk teknologi. Instituttet er også vert for forskningsnettverket Stavanger AI Lab, og tilbyr bachelor- og masterutdanninger i elektroteknikk, datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, kunstig intelligens og medisinsk teknologi. Om arbeidsgiveren:
OM OSS
Vi er Ola og Lars Berbusmel, to brødre med en ekte lidenskap for mat. Ola er bakeren, og Lars er kokken. Vi vokste opp med pappas fisketurer, mammas hjemmebakte brød, mormors fantastiske fiskegrateng og bestefars bløtkaker.

Vår filosofi er enkel: Vi elsker lokale retter og råvarer, rene smaker og å mikse tradisjonelle og moderne teknikker.

For oss er lokal mat en hjertesak. Vi tror på at kortreist mat smaker bedre og samtidig gir noe tilbake til lokalsamfunnet. Derfor samarbeider vi med lokale produsenter for å sikre ferske, bærekraftige råvarer – og for å være med på å bevare og utvikle de tradisjonene vi er så glade i.
BAKERI OG DELIKATESSE
Høsten 2018 åpnet vi vårt eget håndverksbakeri med kafé og delikatessebutikk midt på torget i Bodø. Det er et koselig sted hvor du kan ta en kopp kaffe, holde lunsjmøter eller kjøpe noe ekstra godt til helgen.

Vi legger sjela i håndverket vårt, med fokus på kvalitet og lokale råvarer. Brødene våre bakes med få, men nøye utvalgte ingredienser, og får god tid til å heve – for vi vet at gode ting tar tid.

I delikatesseavdelingen vår finner du produkter vi selv elsker å bruke – fra spekemat og oster til oljer, eddiker og ferskt kjøtt. Vi plukker ut det beste for å gjøre måltidene dine ekstra spesielle.
CATERING
Vi leverer catering til både små og store anledninger. Enten det er bryllup, dåp, konfirmasjon, møter og eventer, en tapaskveld med vennegjengen eller møtemat på jobben, har vi noe for deg.

Våre menyer gjenspeiler sesongen og det vi mener er best akkurat nå. Alt er laget fra bunnen av, med lokale råvarer og leverandører der det er mulig.

About the position
NHH in Bergen, Norway, invites applicants for a tenure-track Assistant Professor or Associate Professor position for seven years in Microeconomics at the Department of Economics.The department has around 50 faculty members and 30 PhD students. It offers an international research environment with a large share of young faculty. The successful candidate will join the Micro research group at the department, a strong academic community with an extensive international network. We expect the candidate to be an active member of the Micro group and to contribute to strengthening the group’s activities, which currently span fields such as industrial organisation, environmental economics, public economics, and microeconomic theory.Other core fields at the department include behavioural economics, development economics, economic history, labour economics and macroeconomics.The department is particularly committed to providing a stimulating and supportive environment for young faculty and offers a dedicated young faculty development programme. For more information, visit our webpage.We are seeking a highly talented candidate with a key interest in microeconomics. A successful candidate should have a strong publication record and/or highly promising work in the pipeline and should also be an excellent teacher with good skills in communicating insights from microeconomics to students. The successful candidate should preferably be able to teach microeconomic theory at all levels. Outreach to society and dissemination of research are also of importance for the position. 
 
To be qualified for the tenure-track position, it should not be more than five years since the PhD degree was achieved (may be extended, for example in connection with statutory leave). For candidates undertaking the PhD, the expected completion of the PhD thesis should be no later than the date of commencement.The position will involve a competitive teaching load, which also includes some graduate student supervision and administrative duties. Faculty members at NHH are expected to be good teachers. NHH offers the opportunity to participate in a program for university pedagogy, and candidates hired for tenure-track position as Assistant Professor must take one basic module of the program during the fixed-term period. Candidates hired for the tenure-track position as Associate Professor, who cannot document at least 200 hours of pedagogical coursework at the time of promotion to a permanent position, must complete this program within two years.NHH values effective communication and expects our faculty to have good language skills in both English and Norwegian. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Assistant Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level (The Common European Framework) within three years of appointment to a permanent position. Candidates hired for a tenure-track position as Associate Professor are required to master proficiency in Norwegian at the B2 level within three years of appointment to the tenure-track position. NHH offers courses in Norwegian for employees who may not initially have Norwegian or another Scandinavian language proficiency.The position is based in Bergen, Norway.
NHH offers
• Annual salary of NOK 726 200 – 784 000 (Assistant Professor) or NOK 784 000 – 840 700 (Associate Professor), depending on the level of competence/length of service. The salary may be adjusted during 2027.
• An academically stimulating working environment.
• A favorable membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) and good welfare benefits such as parental leave.
• Research funds for travel and conference participation, and a bonus system for publication in top international journals (up to NOK 200 000).
• Female associate professors appointed to permanent academic positions may apply for research leave (sabbatical) with half the standard accrual period, in accordance with NHH’s applicable guidelines. This will apply for the first two years of research leave.
Note that public health care, public schooling for children, and most other public services are free in Norway. The city of Bergen has a mild and coastal climate and offers rich opportunities for cultural and outdoor activities as well as a family-friendly environment (explore visitnorway.com). NHH offers dedicated support to international employees. More information about relocation and onboarding services is available on our Onboarding Services webpage.
General information
The appointee must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time. NHH emphasises diversity and encourages qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of gender, age, disability and cultural background.In the assessment of applicants, international experience and qualifications will be emphasised. For the sake of gender balance at NHH, female applicants will be given preference in the event of equivalent qualifications among candidates. The application should contain details of the applicant's scientific and pedagogical education and work experience. In addition, the applicant should provide a teaching statement, which also includes an overview and assessment of the applicants' teaching experience. The application package, including a CV, certificates with grades, a maximum of 5 published or unpublished research papers (for the position of Assistant Professor) or a maximum of 10 published or unpublished research papers (for the position of Associate Professor), a complete list of published papers and papers in the pipeline, and any other relevant documentation, should be submitted through the Jobbnorge online portal. To open the application, please click 'Apply for this job'. For English version, go to the menu at the top right side. 
 
Three reference letters (in PDF) must be submitted by the referees directly to NHH at hr-references@nhh.no by latest 22 December 2026. As part of the recruitment process, a background check may be conducted with the candidates' consent. In accordance with §25 (2) of the Freedom of Information Act, information about applicants may be made public even if they have requested not to have their names entered on the list of applicants. Applicants will be notified if their request is not granted. Enquiries about the position may be directed to:

• Lars Sørgard, Head of Department, email: lars.sorgard@nhh.no
• Morten Sæthre, Professor, email: morten.saethre@nhh.no
• Mette Soltvedt, Administrative Coordinator, email: mette.soltvedt@nhh.no
The deadline for applications is 22 December 2026. This date also applies to the submission of publications/written work.

NHH Norwegian School of Economics is one of the leading business schools in Europe. NHH is the first choice for students who want to study business administration in Norway. jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i metabolitt-MR og nevroavbildning
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i metabolitt-MR og nevroavbildning ved Det teknisk- naturvitenskapelige fakultet, Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi. Stillingen er ledig fra våren 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder fram til doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen opparbeider du kunnskap, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innenfor forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.
 
Den som ansettes tas opp på doktorgradsprogrammet i teknologi og naturvitenskap. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.

Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning eller fire år med forskerutdanning kombinert med annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Dette avklares i rekrutteringsprosessen.

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.
Forskningstema
Den som ansettes vil være tilknyttet forskningsprosjektet BMDLab; Hjernehelse og klinisk nevroavbildning – Undersøkelse av kognitiv svikt ved hjelp av metabolitt-MR og funksjonell MR. Dette prosjektet gjennomføres i tett samarbeid med Stavanger universitetssjukehus (SUS) og har som mål å identifisere tidlige bildediagnostiske biomarkører for kognitiv svikt ved normal aldring og ved kliniske tilstander, som mild kognitiv svikt og Alzheimers sykdom. Datainnsamlingen er allerede i gang ved hjelp av den nylig installerte 3T Siemens MAGNETOM Cima.X, utstyrt med Gemini-gradientsystemet. Dette systemet tilbyr toppmoderne ytelse for avanserte nevroavbildningsprotokoller, inkludert MR-spektroskopisk avbildning og funksjonell MR (fMRI) med høy oppløsning.

Multimodal avbildning gir en unik mulighet til å forstå ulike deler av hjernen i sammenheng med kognitiv svikt ved aldring og sykdom. Magnetisk resonansspektroskopi (MRS) gjør det mulig å måle metabolitter i hjernen på en ikke-invasiv måte, blant annet GABA og glutamat. Konsentrasjonene av disse stoffene kan fungere som sensitive markører for tidlige tegn på nevrodegenerasjon og kognitiv svikt. Funksjonell MR supplerer disse målingene ved å undersøke hjernens funksjon gjennom endringer i blodets oksygentilførsel under ulike kognitive tilstander. Dette omfatter både hviletilstand og mer naturlige opplevelser, som for eksempel å se på film. Tidligere forskning tyder på at individuelle forskjeller i konsentrasjonen av metabolitter i hjernen henger sammen med forskjeller i hjernens funksjonelle integritet. Et sentralt spørsmål står imidlertid fortsatt ubesvart: Er endringer i disse metabolittene relatert til endringer i hjernens funksjon, og hvordan bidrar disse sammenhengene til kognitiv svikt? Dette doktorgradsprosjektet vil kombinere MRS, fMRI og kognitive undersøkelser for å studere sammenhengen mellom hjernens metabolisme, funksjonell organisering og kognitiv svikt.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha en sterk faglig bakgrunn med femårig mastergrad innenfor biofysikk, medisinsk teknologi, biomedisinsk ingeniørfag eller tilsvarende fagområder, eller tilsvarende utdanning som gir grunnlag for å gjennomføre en forskerutdanning, fortrinnsvis av nyere dato.

Karakter på masteroppgaven og veid gjennomsnittskarakter for masterstudiet må begge tilsvare B eller bedre. 

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.

Dersom du fullfører mastergraden våren 2027, er du også velkommen til å søke.
 
Vi legger også vekt på at du:

• har sterk interesse for klinisk nevrovitenskap: du bør være komfortabel med å delta i MR-undersøkelser, har stor interesse for nevroavbildning og særlig for verktøy for multimodale data (f.eks. SPM, FSL, osv.). Du bør også ha gode ferdigheter i bruk av avanserte statistiske og multivariate metoder for analyse av komplekse nevroavbildningsdata.
• har erfaring med kognitiv testing, signalbehandling og/eller bildeanalyse.
• har motivasjon for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og tverrfaglig samarbeid.
• er intellektuelt nysgjerrig, initiativrik og har evne til kritisk refleksjon, nytenkning og selvstendig problemløsning.
• har potensial for forskning innenfor fagfeltet og personlige forutsetninger for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• kan arbeide godt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• har evne til kritisk refleksjon, nytenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, og arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø.
• har gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig.Krav til engelskkunnskaper
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk, både skriftlig og muntlig, er en forutsetning for opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet.

Du er fritatt fra kravet dersom du:

I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  

Universitetet ønsker bedre kjønnsbalanse i stipendiatstillinger innenfor fagområdet og oppfordrer derfor særlig kvinner til å søke. Ved tilnærmet like kvalifikasjoner kan kvinner bli prioritert i samsvar med gjeldende regelverk.

• motivasjonsbrev (maks. 400 ord) som beskriver dine forskningsinteresser, motivasjonen for å søke stillingen og relevansen av din bakgrunn for det aktuelle forskningsprosjektet.
• CV med fullstendig oversikt over utdanning, erfaring og eventuell vitenskapelig virksomhet

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. UiS behandler bare søknader og vedlegg registrert i Jobbnorge.

Opplysninger om søkere kan bli offentliggjort selv om det er bedt om unntak fra offentlig søkerliste, jf. offentlighetsloven § 25. Dersom anmodningen ikke tas til følge, vil du bli varslet.

UiS er underlagt sikkerhetsloven, og det forventes at ansatte utviser sikkerhetsbevisst atferd, og følger gjeldende sikkerhets- og eksportkontrollrutiner. Ved ansettelse vil egenskaper som pålitelighet, dømmekraft og lojalitet bli vektlagt.

Ansettelse som stipendiat er regulert i universitets- og høgskoleforskriften kapittel IV. Opptak til doktorgradsutdanningen er regulert i forskrift for graden philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) ved Universitetet i Stavanger.

Dine kvalifikasjoner for stillingen vil bli vurdert av en intern komité på grunnlag av dokumentasjonen registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristens utløp. Doktorgradsarbeidet skal i hovedsak gjennomføres ved Universitetet i Stavanger. Det er en forutsetning at den som ansettes bosetter seg slik at vedkommende kan være til stede og tilgjengelig for fagmiljøet i ordinær arbeidstid.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den engelske teksten som legges til grunn.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Universitetet i Stavanger (UiS) har omlag 12.000 studenter og 2.200 ansatte. Universitetet har store ambisjoner. Vi skal ha en innovativ og internasjonal profil og være en drivkraft i kunnskapsutviklingen og endringsprosesser i samfunnet. Vår felles retning skal drives frem av omtanke for grønn og bærekraftig omstilling og rettferdig samfunnsutvikling, gjennom nye måter å forvalte naturressursene på og legge til rette for bedre byer og lokalsamfunn. Energi, helse og velferd, læring for livet er våre satsingsområder.I samspill og dialog med våre omgivelser regionalt, nasjonalt og internasjonalt har vi et åpent og innovativt klima for utdanning, forskning, kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid, nyskapning, formidling og museumsvirksomhet. Den faglige virksomheten ved universitetet er organisert i seks fakultet med 13 institutt og to nasjonale forsknings- og kompetansesenter i tillegg til Arkeologisk museum. Vi er medlem i det europeiske nettverket for innovative universitet - European Consortium of Innovative Universities. Universitetet ligger i den mest attraktive regionen i landet med 300.000 innbyggere.  Stavangerregionen har et dynamisk arbeidsmarked og tilbyr en rekke spennende kultur- og fritidsaktiviteter.Sammen med våre ansatte og studenter vil vi løfte blikket, og våge å tenke stort og nytt – vi vil utfordre det velkjente og utforske det ukjente.

Det teknisk-naturvitenskapelige fakultet tilbyr utdanninger på bachelor-, master- og doktorgradsnivå. Fakultetet har sterke bånd til både forskningsinstitusjoner og industri. Nesten 40 % av budsjettet er eksternt finansiert. Studentene våre har tett kontakt med næringslivet, og mange master- og doktorgradsoppgaver blir skrevet i samarbeid med industrien. Fakultetet har etablert forskningssamarbeid med universiteter over hele verden, og har flere fagmiljø som er internasjonalt ledende. Fakultetet har om lag 3000 studenter og rundt 500 ansatte fordelt på fakultetsadministrasjonen og seks institutt: institutt for data- og elektroteknikk, institutt for maskin, bygg og materialteknologi, institutt for matematikk og fysikk, institutt for kjemi, biovitenskap og miljøteknologi, institutt for energi- og petroleumsteknologi og institutt for sikkerhet, økonomi og planlegging. Institutt for data- og elektroteknologi driver forskning innen datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, elkraft, signalbehandling og medisinsk teknologi. Instituttet er også vert for forskningsnettverket Stavanger AI Lab, og tilbyr bachelor- og masterutdanninger i elektroteknikk, datateknologi, data science, kybernetikk, kunstig intelligens og medisinsk teknologi. I tillegg tilbys ph.d.-utdanning i de samme fagområdene.

We build industrial intelligence software for heavy-asset sectors. As a KONGSBERG company backed by over 200 years of heritage, Falkor helps the energy, chemicals, utilities and other industrial sectors operate with absolute clarity, confidence, and control.

Our AI-enabled platform connects people, systems, and workflows—expanding human capability by turning complex data into real-time, actionable decisions. We help leading organizations improve safety, efficiency and performance while redefining how heavy assets are designed and operated.

Help turn marketing into commercial momentum at Falkor
Falkor is looking for an experienced and hands-on Demand Generation & Events Manager to join our Marketing team on a temporary basis.

You’ll lead our Demand Generation & Events function, manage a team of two, and take ownership of our global demand generation campaigns and events program. Working closely with colleagues across Marketing, Sales/Growth and our regional teams, you’ll help ensure our marketing investments translate into measurable engagement, opportunities and pipeline.

This is a role for someone who enjoys combining people leadership, strategy and hands-on execution. You’ll step into an established function with ongoing campaigns, events and plans, while having plenty of opportunity to bring your own experience and ideas.

Lead the Demand Generation & Events team

• 
Translate Falkor’s commercial and marketing priorities into a focused demand generation and events plan.

• 
Prioritize resources and investment across campaigns, markets, and events based on expected impact.

• 
Build effective ways of working across Marketing and with our commercial and regional teams.

• 
Combine team leadership with hands-on involvement when needed.

Drive demand generation

Plan, execute and optimize integrated demand generation campaigns across paid and organic channels.

Work closely with Product Marketing, content and commercial teams to develop campaigns for priority audiences, markets and offerings.

Experience from B2B technology, SaaS, industrial technology, or energy would be an advantage.

You'll be joining a global technology company helping to redefine how complex industries operate.
